newsitem.title: USA: Saratoga County sets budget, raises taxes - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saratoga County sets budget, raises taxes - paper.

text.p: Saratoga County, N.Y., supervisors approved a 1997 budget that totals around $123.8 million, down $6 million from the current budget, though it raises property taxes four percent, the Daily Gazette said in its Thursday edition.
The paper quoted county officials as saying that the budget, which is expected to increase taxes by $11.66 for a home assessed at $108,000, produced no complaints at public hearings.
Saratoga's Law and Finance Committee Chairman Marvn LeRoy said the county has the lowest taxes per captia of any county in the state. Saratoga County cut taxes 10 percent in the 1996 budget.
The new budget cut two administrative-level positions, while creating two new corrections officer spots at the county jail, along with two part-time jail nurses slots.
One county supervisor, the only Democrat, Christopher Sgambati, voted against the budget, criticizing a plan to spend $9 million on a landfill fund and high administrative salaries, the paper said.
Actual tax rates for the 19 towns and two cities areexpected to be rady for adoption by the Board of Supervisors at a meeting on Tuesday.
